input: Swap out the shower head for a rainfall one

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Rainfall heads vary hugely — ceiling-mounted fixed panels require pipe rerouting, while arm-mounted drop-down versions are near plug-and-play. The scope of work changes entirely depending on which type they want.
The existing shower setup (overhead fixed pipe, standard wall arm, or handheld) determines compatibility and what adapters or new hardware are needed.
Rainfall heads range from ~$30 to $500+. Budget affects which product to buy and whether a plumber is needed vs. a DIY fix.
Knowing whether the user is doing this themselves or hiring a tradesperson changes what the plan looks like — tool lists vs. brief search.
If DIY, knowing what tools they already have (adjustable wrench, plumber's tape, etc.) determines what they need to gather before starting.
Finish (chrome, matte black, brushed nickel) and head size affect the product recommendation and whether it matches existing bathroom fixtures.
Some users just want it functional; others want no leaks, matching aesthetics, and strong water pressure. This shapes how thorough the plan needs to be.

gold.taskTitle: Replace existing shower head with rainfall one
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to remove their current shower head and install a new rainfall-style shower head in their home.

questions.title: What style of rainfall head do you want fitted?
questions.description: Ceiling-mounted flush panel, extended ceiling arm, or a wall-arm drop-down head — each has very different installation complexity.

questions.title: What does your current shower setup look like?
questions.description: Is there a standard wall-mounted arm, a fixed overhead pipe, or a handheld hose? This determines compatibility with the new head.

questions.title: Are you doing this yourself or hiring a plumber?
questions.description: DIY vs. hiring a tradesperson completely changes the action plan — tool checklist and steps vs. how to brief a professional.

questions.title: What is your budget for the new shower head?
questions.description: Entry-level models start around $30; high-end ones exceed $300. Budget narrows down which products to recommend.

questions.title: Which tools do you already have at home?
questions.description: Knowing if you have an adjustable wrench, plumber's tape (PTFE), and a cloth avoids redundant steps and flags what to buy first.

questions.title: What finish or size do you prefer for the new head?
questions.description: Chrome, matte black, brushed nickel, and head diameter (8" vs. 12"+) affect the product search and visual match with existing fixtures.

questions.title: What does a successful install look like to you?
questions.description: Is the priority just getting it working, or do you also need strong pressure, zero leaks, and a finish that matches the rest of the bathroom?
